info.name: Chat Dashboard - Backend 2 (staff API)
info.description: Sign in first: Auth and accounts > 'Sign in (staff)' saves {{token}} (create the first admin with `pnpm --filter @chat-dashboard/backend user:create-admin`). With AUTH_MODE=dev you can instead set token to dev:<userId>:<ROLE>, e.g. dev:00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000004:AGENT. Other tokens: dev:00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000004:AGENT, dev:00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000009:SUPERVISOR. Run 'Create' first, then 'Take over' before sending messages. FR-14 to FR-27 folders were added in the enhanced-chat work: run Conversations > Create, Assignment > Take over, Messages > Send first; most requests then work with the saved variables. Customer-side calls, moderation enforcement and the file/voice uploads need a customer channel or files, see docs/api-*.md.

item.name: Auth and accounts
item.description: Sign-in, tokens and account management. See docs/api-auth.md.

request.description: Public. Create the first admin with `pnpm --filter @chat-dashboard/backend user:create-admin`. Saves {{token}} and {{refreshToken}}.

item.name: Sign in with LOS (staff) - saves token

request.description: Public. Exchanges the short-lived LOS staff hand-off token (RS256; aud=LOS_HANDOFF_AUDIENCE, type=staff, tokenType=LOS_HANDOFF_TOKEN_TYPE, role) for this backend's tokens. 503 LOS_SIGN_IN_DISABLED when LOS_ISSUER is not set. Saves {{token}} and {{refreshToken}}.
Public. Rotates: the old refresh token stops working. Replaying a used one revokes the whole sign-in.
Public, always 204.
Revokes every refresh token of the caller.
The signed-in account.
Signs out other devices; returns a new sign-in.
Supervisors and admins.
Admins only.
Supervisors and admins.
Needs users.manage (admins by default). DISABLED or a new role signs the user out.
Admins only. Signs the user out everywhere.
Needs roles.read (supervisors and admins by default). See docs/api-roles.md.
Every permission a role can have, as module.action. Needs roles.read.

Needs roles.manage (admins by default). Replaces the whole set; ADMIN must keep users.manage and roles.manage; customer roles get none. Applies within 60 s. The example targets AGENT (roleId 2), which starts with none, so running it changes nothing; list permission keys (e.g. "conversations.view_all") to widen it.
Public. Creates a CUSTOMER and signs them in.
Public. Staff accounts are refused here.

item.name: Sign in with LOS (customer) - saves customerToken

request.description: Public. Exchanges the LOS customer access token the app holds (RS256; aud=LOS_CUSTOMER_AUDIENCE, type=customer, tokenType=access). Creates an account without email or password on the first sign-in. Saves {{customerToken}} and {{customerRefreshToken}}.
Public.
Public, always 204.
Revokes every refresh token of the customer. `204`.
Signs out other devices; returns a new sign-in.

item.name: Take over again (the next folders need an owner)

request.description: Receipts exist only for customer messages: use a customer message id (`400` for an agent message such as {{msgId}}).
Runs as agent 4 (AUTH_MODE=dev), who was notified of the assignment above; use your own token otherwise.
Runs as agent 4 (AUTH_MODE=dev), who was notified of the assignment above; use your own token otherwise.

HIGH, MEDIUM or LOW (new conversations start at MEDIUM). The owner, a supervisor, or anyone while nobody owns the conversation (`permissions.canOrganize`). The same value is a no-op. Adds a `PRIORITY_CHANGED` timeline entry and broadcasts `conversation.priority_changed`. Two simultaneous changes: one wins, the other gets 409.
Sends an agent message with `replyToMessageId` set. Same rules as sending (owner of an open conversation) and same idempotency by `clientId`. Delivered as `message.new`.
Author only, text messages only, while the caller still owns the open conversation. The previous text is saved in the edit history. Unchanged text is a no-op. Broadcast as `message.updated`.
Earlier versions, newest edit first. Only the author and supervisors may read it.
Idempotent: the same emoji twice keeps one reaction. At most 10 different emojis per user and message (409). Anyone who can see the conversation may react. Broadcast as `message.reaction_updated`.

exec: const id = d.id || (d.reactions && d.reactions.length ? d.reactions[0].id : null);

request.description: Only the reaction's owner (403 otherwise). Broadcast as `message.reaction_updated`.

Copies a text message into another conversation the caller owns and that is open, keeping `forwardedFromMessageId`. Allowed only within the same customer's conversations or into an internal conversation. Idempotent by `clientId`. Broadcast as `message.new` plus `message.forwarded`.

Soft delete (the row and its history are kept). Authors delete their own messages; supervisors and admins any agent, AI or customer message. SYSTEM messages cannot be deleted. Broadcast as `message.deleted`.

Multipart: `file`, `conversationId`, `clientId`, optional `text` caption. Stores the file and sends a message carrying it (type IMAGE, FILE, AUDIO or VIDEO). Allowed: JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP, PDF, TXT, CSV, DOC(X), XLS(X), MP3, OGG, WAV, WebM, M4A, MP4, MOV. The MIME type, the extension and the file's first bytes must agree; images 10 MB, other files up to 25 MB. Only the owner of an open conversation. Idempotent by `clientId` (200 on a retry). Broadcast as `message.new` and `attachment.uploaded`. If storing the message fails, the stored file is removed.

Multipart: `file` (an audio recording, max 10 MB), `clientId`, optional `durationMs` (measured by the browser, up to 10 minutes) and `waveform` (a JSON array of up to 200 integers 0 to 255). The message has type VOICE. Same rules as sending a file.
Newest first. Filter with `kind`: image, document, audio, video or voice. Deleted files are not listed.

Streams the file after checking the caller may see its conversation. Needs the bearer token, so the browser fetches it and shows the bytes from a blob URL. `?inline=1` displays images, audio and video; every other type is always sent as a download. Supports one `Range` (206) so audio and video can seek. Sent with `Cache-Control: private`, `nosniff` and a sandbox CSP.
The audio of a voice or audio message, streamed inline with `Range` support.
The uploader or a supervisor/admin. The record is kept (soft delete) and the stored bytes are removed. Broadcast as `attachment.deleted`. Deleting the message removes its files the same way.
Newest first. Anyone who may see the conversation can read its notes. Notes are staff-only and are never part of message history or any customer-facing API.

Anyone who may see the conversation. `mentionedAgentIds` lists the agents to notify; each must exist in Backend 1 and be able to open the conversation (400 otherwise, `error.details.agentIds` names them). Mentioning yourself is ignored. Adds a `NOTE_ADDED` timeline entry (without the text). Broadcast as `note.created`, and `note.mentioned` plus a `MENTION` notification for each mentioned agent.

exec: const id = d.id || (d.reactions && d.reactions.length ? d.reactions[0].id : null);

request.description: Author only. `text` and/or the complete new `mentionedAgentIds`; only agents added by this edit are notified. Broadcast as `note.updated`.
The author, or a supervisor/admin. Soft delete. Broadcast as `note.deleted`.
Alphabetical, with how many conversations use each. `q` searches the name.
Any agent. The name is unique ignoring case (409). `color` is `#RRGGBB`.

exec: const id = d.id || (d.reactions && d.reactions.length ? d.reactions[0].id : null);

request.description: The tag's creator or a supervisor. `color: null` clears the color. Conversations using the tag receive `conversation.tags_updated`.

Replaces the conversation's tags with `tagIds` (at most 20; an empty list removes all). The owner, a supervisor, or anyone while nobody owns the conversation (`permissions.canOrganize`). Unknown ids give 400. Additions and removals are recorded as `TAG_ADDED`/`TAG_REMOVED`, and `conversation.tags_updated` is broadcast. Idempotent.

Supervisors only. A tag used by conversations is refused with 409 (`error.details.usageCount`) unless `force=true`, which takes it off every conversation first (a `TAG_REMOVED` timeline entry on each) and then deletes it. `409` while conversations use the tag unless `force=true` (shown here).

Your personal templates and the shared ones, active only, by title. `q` searches title, text and shortcut; `shortcut` finds one by what the agent typed; `includeInactive` also lists deactivated templates you could reactivate. Other agents' personal templates are never listed.

`scope` PERSONAL (default; private to you) or SHARED (supervisors/admins only; visible to everyone). `shortcut` like `/greeting` must be free among the templates you can see (409). TEAM templates are not available yet.

exec: const id = d.id || (d.reactions && d.reactions.length ? d.reactions[0].id : null);

request.description: Someone else's personal template answers 404, as if it did not exist.

item.name: Edit, deactivate or reactivate a template

request.description: Your own personal template, or a shared one if you are a supervisor/admin (403 otherwise). The scope cannot change. `shortcut: null` removes the shortcut; `isActive` false/true deactivates/reactivates.
Templates are never deleted: this deactivates it (same rights as editing) and frees its shortcut. Repeating it changes nothing.
Newest first, including resolved and cancelled ones.

Only the owner of a conversation that is not closed. One escalation can be pending at a time (409). Adds an `ESCALATED` timeline entry and broadcasts `conversation.escalated` to everyone who can see the conversation. It does not change the owner, status or priority.

exec: const id = d.id || (d.reactions && d.reactions.length ? d.reactions[0].id : null);

request.description: `RESOLVED`: supervisors and admins. `CANCELLED`: the requester or a supervisor. A closed escalation cannot change again (409). Broadcast as `conversation.escalated` with the new status.

Everything needed to restore the dashboard: tab preferences, the tabs left open (empty when `restoreTabs` is off) with each conversation's current state and this agent's unread count, and unsent drafts. Conversations the agent can no longer see are omitted.
Partial update; omitted keys keep their value. Broadcast as `workspace.preferences_updated`.

Idempotent: an open tab is only refreshed, so two windows never create a duplicate. Needs access to the conversation. With `persistTabs` off nothing is stored and `persisted` is false. At most 20 tabs (409). Broadcast as `workspace.tab_opened`. This never changes the conversation itself.
Idempotent. Only removes the tab: the conversation is not closed, resolved or archived. Broadcast as `workspace.tab_closed` when a tab was removed.

Replaces my unsent text for this conversation (max 10000 characters). Drafts are per agent and conversation. An empty `content` deletes the draft and returns `null`. Broadcast as `workspace.draft_updated`.
Idempotent. Call after the message was sent. Broadcast as `workspace.draft_updated` with `content: null`.
The caller's own switches. Defaults are returned until something was saved (sounds and AI on, auto-assign off); reading never creates a row.

Partial update; omitted keys keep their value, unknown keys are rejected. Only the caller's settings can be changed. Broadcast to the caller's other sessions as `chat_settings.updated`. The AI and auto-assign switches are stored only: nothing reads them yet.
Callbacks assigned to me or scheduled by me, soonest first. Filters: `status`, `from`/`to` (scheduled time, ISO 8601 with offset). `scope=all` lists everyone's and is for supervisors (403 otherwise).
Every callback of the conversation in any status, soonest first. Needs access to the conversation.

Anyone who can see the conversation. `scheduledAt` must be in the future (at most 365 days) and carry a UTC offset. The assignee defaults to the conversation's owner, else the caller; another agent must exist and be able to see the conversation. At most 20 pending per conversation (409). Notifies the assignee when it is someone else, adds a `CALLBACK` timeline entry and broadcasts `callback.created`.

exec: const id = d.id || (d.reactions && d.reactions.length ? d.reactions[0].id : null);

request.description: Its assignee, its creator, supervisors, or anyone who can see the conversation. Otherwise 404.

Assignee, creator or supervisor, on a PENDING or MISSED callback (409 once completed or cancelled). A new `scheduledAt` makes it PENDING again and allows a new reminder. Changing `assignedAgentId` notifies the new assignee. Broadcast as `callback.updated`.
Assignee, creator or supervisor. From PENDING or MISSED (a late call still counts). 409 if already closed. Broadcast as `callback.completed`.

Anyone who can see the conversation. `scheduledAt` must be in the future (at most 365 days) and carry a UTC offset. The assignee defaults to the conversation's owner, else the caller; another agent must exist and be able to see the conversation. At most 20 pending per conversation (409). Notifies the assignee when it is someone else, adds a `CALLBACK` timeline entry and broadcasts `callback.created`.

exec: const id = d.id || (d.reactions && d.reactions.length ? d.reactions[0].id : null);

request.description: Assignee, creator or supervisor. From PENDING or MISSED. 409 if already closed. Broadcast as `callback.cancelled`.

STUN and TURN servers for `RTCPeerConnection`. TURN credentials are short-lived and specific to the caller when a shared secret is configured. Responds with `Cache-Control: no-store`. Empty `iceServers` means none are configured (calls then only work on the same network).
Newest first, any status. Needs access to the conversation.

Only the owner of a conversation that is not closed. The call starts `RINGING`; a conversation can have one call that is not over (409). Adds a `CALL` timeline entry and sends `call.incoming` to the customer's channel. After `call.accepted`, the caller sends the offer over the WebSocket (`call.offer`). Unanswered calls become `MISSED` after the ring timeout.

exec: const id = d.id || (d.reactions && d.reactions.length ? d.reactions[0].id : null);

request.description: Needs access to the call's conversation (otherwise 404).

A ringing call a customer started: a supervisor, the owner, or any agent while nobody owns the conversation. The first to answer wins; the others get 409. The answering agent becomes a participant. Broadcast as `call.accepted`. Only for a call the customer started (customer calls have no REST channel yet), so `403` for the call started above.
Same people as accept. The call becomes `DECLINED`. Broadcast as `call.declined`. Only for a call the customer started (customer calls have no REST channel yet), so `403` for the call started above.
Only the caller, and only while it rings. The call becomes `CANCELLED`. Broadcast as `call.ended` with reason `cancelled`.
A participant, or a supervisor, on an answered call. Records the duration. Broadcast as `call.ended` with reason `ended`. For an accepted call; `409` after the call above was cancelled.

The owner of the conversation, or a supervisor. The customer comes from the conversation. 409 if already blocked. Records the action in the moderation log and on the conversation timeline, and broadcasts `customer.blocked`. Open conversations stay open; the block stops what the customer does (messages, calls) once the customer channel exists.
Supervisors only. 409 if already blocked.
A supervisor, or the agent who blocked the customer. Anyone else gets 404 (they cannot tell whether the customer is blocked).
Current blocks (`active=false` for lifted ones), newest first. Supervisors see all; an agent sees the blocks they made. `customerName` comes from Backend 1 and is null when it cannot be reached.
Every keyword (active or not), alphabetical. Any dashboard user can read them. A message from a customer containing an active keyword (ignoring case) is stored and flagged for review, never rejected.
Supervisors only. Unique ignoring case (409). At most 1000 active keywords.

exec: const id = d.id || (d.reactions && d.reactions.length ? d.reactions[0].id : null);

request.description: Supervisors only. Takes effect within about 15 seconds on every API instance.
Supervisors only. Deletes it for good (the log keeps its text).

Anyone who can see the conversation, about the conversation or one of its messages (`messageId`, which must belong to it). One pending report per reporter and target (409). Broadcast as `spam.reported` to whoever can see the conversation, which includes supervisors. Optional `messageId` (a message of this conversation) points at the offending message.

exec: const id = d.id || (d.reactions && d.reactions.length ? d.reactions[0].id : null);

request.description: Anyone who can see the conversation. Newest first.
Supervisors see every report (filter by `status`, usually `PENDING`); an agent sees the ones they filed.

Supervisors only. A reviewed report cannot be reviewed again (409). With `CONFIRMED`, `blockCustomer: true` also blocks the conversation's customer in the same transaction (a customer who is already blocked stays blocked). Broadcast as `spam.reviewed`.
Supervisors only. Who blocked, unblocked, reported, reviewed or changed keywords, newest first. Filter by `targetType` or `actorId`.

item.name: Mobile (customer) API
item.description: Customer mobile app. Dev auth: Bearer dev:<customerUuid>:CUSTOMER (AUTH_MODE=dev). Run 'Join room' first: it saves the conversation id to {{customerConvId}} (set it from the response). See docs/api-customer-mobile.md.

request.description: The signed-in staff user and their availability.
Conversations the agent owns; inbox filters except `filter`.
